flow-api-concept.title: Backpressure with the Flow API
flow-api-concept.short: Model asynchronous exchange between publishers and subscribers
flow-api-concept.summary: The Flow API defines Publisher, Subscriber, Subscription, and related interfaces for asynchronous data exchange with flow control.
flow-api-concept.why: Subscribers can request an amount they are ready to process instead of requiring publishers to push without a demand signal.
flow-api-concept.tips: Flow defines the protocol; consider SubmissionPublisher or a compatible library according to the application's needs.

stack-walker-concept.title: Inspect call stacks with StackWalker
stack-walker-concept.short: Traverse only the stack frames you need
stack-walker-concept.summary: StackWalker provides a lazy API for traversing stack frames of the current thread.
stack-walker-concept.why: It can search or process selected frames without first materializing the entire stack as an array.
stack-walker-concept.tips: Request options such as retained class references only when the additional information is needed.

files-mismatch.title: Compare files with Files.mismatch
files-mismatch.short: Find the first differing byte position
files-mismatch.summary: Files.mismatch compares two files and returns the position of their first differing byte, or -1 when their contents match.
files-mismatch.why: It avoids writing a manual loop that reads and compares the files yourself.
files-mismatch.tips: It compares file contents, not metadata such as modification times or permissions.

collectors-teeing.title: Combine two aggregations with Collectors.teeing
collectors-teeing.short: Feed the same input to two collectors and merge their results
collectors-teeing.summary: teeing sends every input element to two downstream collectors and combines their final results with a merger function.
collectors-teeing.why: It expresses tasks such as obtaining both a minimum and maximum from one stream in a single collect operation.
collectors-teeing.tips: For simple numerical statistics, a summarizing collector may communicate the intent more directly.

unchecked-io-exception.title: UncheckedIOException
unchecked-io-exception.short: Carry an I/O failure as an unchecked exception
unchecked-io-exception.summary: UncheckedIOException is an unchecked exception that retains an IOException as its cause.
unchecked-io-exception.why: It can propagate I/O failure through functional operations whose signatures do not directly allow checked IOException.
unchecked-io-exception.tips: When catching it, inspect getCause so the underlying IOException remains available for diagnosis and handling.

invalid-path-exception.title: InvalidPathException
invalid-path-exception.short: Handle strings that cannot be converted to paths
invalid-path-exception.summary: InvalidPathException is thrown when a string cannot be interpreted as a valid path for the active file system.
invalid-path-exception.why: Valid path syntax and characters can differ between environments, so creating a Path from external text can fail.
invalid-path-exception.tips: For user input, convert the exception into useful validation feedback instead of hard-coding one operating system's path rules.

record-extends-class-error.title: A record cannot extend another class
record-extends-class-error.short: A record's superclass is implicitly Record
record-extends-class-error.summary: A record class implicitly extends java.lang.Record, so declaring another superclass with extends is a compile-time error.
record-extends-class-error.why: The language fixes the structural model of records as data-carrier classes.
record-extends-class-error.tips: When a shared type contract is needed, consider implementing an interface rather than inheriting from a class.

lambda-checked-exception-error.title: Checked exceptions in lambdas must match the target type
lambda-checked-exception-error.short: Use an interface whose abstract method permits the exception
lambda-checked-exception-error.summary: A lambda cannot throw a checked exception that the abstract method of its target functional interface does not permit.
lambda-checked-exception-error.why: For example, Runnable.run has no throws clause, so an operation that throws IOException cannot be mapped to it unchanged.
lambda-checked-exception-error.tips: Choose a suitable functional interface or handle the checked exception inside the lambda.

for-removal-deprecation-warning.title: Deprecation warning for APIs marked for removal
for-removal-deprecation-warning.short: Migrate away from APIs whose forRemoval flag is true
for-removal-deprecation-warning.summary: An API annotated as Deprecated with forRemoval=true is intended to be removed in a future release.
for-removal-deprecation-warning.why: It is a stronger signal than ordinary deprecation because continued compatibility with that API should not be assumed.
for-removal-deprecation-warning.tips: Check deprecation warnings and API documentation, then migrate to the documented replacement before removal.

optional-map-null-empty-trap.title: Optional.map turns null results into empty
optional-map-null-empty-trap.short: A mapping function cannot preserve null as a contained value
optional-map-null-empty-trap.summary: When an Optional.map function returns null, the result is Optional.empty rather than an Optional containing null.
optional-map-null-empty-trap.why: Optional does not store null as a present value, and map treats a null mapping result as absence.
optional-map-null-empty-trap.tips: Avoid relying on null-producing transformations; represent an absent transformation result deliberately with Optional.
